dicas.texto: Você está indo muito bem! Pense: quantas vezes o número 7 cabe dentro do 9?
Tente dividir 9 por 7. O quociente será o seu número inteiro (m1) e o resto será o novo numerador (m2). O denominador (m3) permanece o mesmo.
O número inteiro (m1) é 1, porque 7 cabe uma vez em 9. Agora, subtraia 7 de 9 para descobrir o que sobra para o numerador (m2).
Você quase conseguiu! Se você tirou um grupo de 7/7 de 9/7, quanto sobra de numerador? O denominador continua sendo 7. Então, preencha m1=1, m2=2 e m3=7.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem? Convert it to mixed fraction form if it will help you." com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); botão "Convert" que abre as caixas do número misto (m1 = parte inteira, m2/m3 = fração restante; "-" quando não há); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 7 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

For a fraction, place the amount being measured in the top box.
The story says that Eric finished the project in nine days.
Type the number of days Eric took into the top box.
Ask what unit the fraction is describing and how many days make that unit.
Use the number of days in one week as the denominator.
A week is made of seven days.
Type the number of days in one week into the bottom box.
Compare the numerator with the denominator to decide how many wholes the fraction contains.
A fraction is greater than one when its numerator is greater than its denominator.
Compare 9 with 7 and use the fraction model to represent the original fraction.
Show nine parts when each whole is divided into seven equal parts.
A mixed number shows the complete wholes and the fractional part that remains.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the whole number and the remainder.
Seven fits into nine one time, leaving two parts, and the denominator stays 7.
Enter one whole, then write the remaining two parts over seven parts in the mixed-number fields.
Use the mixed-number form to locate the fraction after one whole.
Start at 1 and move two of the seven equal intervals toward 2.
The target is two sevenths beyond 1, not two sevenths beyond 0.
Place the point at the second seventh mark to the right of 1.
Before submitting, check that the point matches both the original fraction and its mixed-number form.
Verify the point is two sevenths after 1 on the number line.
Confirm that the marked location represents 9/7 rather than a point before 1.
When the point shows one whole and two sevenths, click the Done button.

hints.message: Use the mixed-number form to locate the fraction after one whole.
Start at 1 and move two of the seven equal intervals toward 2.
The target is two sevenths beyond 1, not two sevenths beyond 0.
Place the point at the second seventh mark to the right of 1.

nodes.description: After checking the point, click Done.

hints.message: Before submitting, check that the point matches both the original fraction and its mixed-number form.
Verify the point is two sevenths after 1 on the number line.
Confirm that the marked location represents 9/7 rather than a point before 1.
When the point shows one whole and two sevenths, click the Done button.
